title: Trump Amplifies Elon Musk’s False “Welfare for Illegal Immigrants” Posts (2024)
description_short: Trump Amplifies Elon Musk’s False “Welfare for Illegal Immigrants” Posts (2024)
notes: Focused read of the linked NBC News story by David Ingram, published August 12, 2024 and updated that evening, covers the live Trump–Musk X discussion: it began about 40 minutes late, lasted more than two hours, and X reported a peak of more than 1.3 million listeners. The story describes their shared opposition to immigration and Trump’s repeated claim that the Congo had emptied prisons and sent prisoners to the United States. It does not mention the alleged welfare-benefit posts, benefit amounts, campaign use, or claimed reach. Still needed: the specific posts and dates, evidence for the programs and amounts, and evidence of the alleged campaign amplification and reach.

title: Trump Fires Three Members of US Sentencing Commission on Day One
description_short: Trump Fires Three Members of US Sentencing Commission on Day One
description_medium: The linked U.S. Sentencing Commission press-release archive describes the Commission as an independent agency in the judicial branch created by the Sentencing Reform Act of 1984. It says commissioners are nominated by the President and confirmed by the Senate. The archive does not identify commissioners removed on January 20, 2025, or document a removal action. The supplied link therefore provides institutional context but does not verify the event in the title.
notes: Focused read of the U.S. Sentencing Commission’s official Press Releases archive confirmed its institutional description: an independent judicial-branch agency created in 1984, with commissioners nominated by the President and confirmed by the Senate; the Attorney General or designee and Parole Commission chair are ex-officio nonvoting members. The archive page contains no case-specific notice identifying the three alleged removals or their date. Still needed: commissioner names and removal notices or contemporaneous reporting, plus the statute or filing establishing any for-cause protection.
